routing_warnings.description: The requested changes concern the strapline's visual prominence, color treatment, and surrounding lines rather than its wording.
The selected graduated-color treatment for the strapline changes visual styling rather than logo wording.
The requested changes affect the shapes and relative heights of letters in the existing word DOUGH, not the required wording.
The request for versions with and without the black box belongs to the boxed and unboxed logo-variant Requirement.
The request to receive multiple color variants belongs to the color-variant delivery Requirement; only the selected primary color treatment affects the target visual design.
The PNG opening failures concern usable raster-file delivery rather than the logo's visual composition.
The AI, EPS, and PSD compatibility concerns belong to editable vector and source-file delivery.
The request for a complementary website and heading font belongs to brand typography guidance.
The request concerns written confirmation of copyright ownership for a future trademark application, not the originality of the logo artwork.
The message verifies PNG display behavior and explains background-color blending; it does not verify delivery of both boxed and unboxed logo variants.
The reported problem concerns whether the PNG files open and display correctly, not the required set of color variants.
The delivery of color codes supports the brand color specification rather than delivery of the full-color, black, and white logo variants.
The selected primary-logo color treatment concerns application of colors within the logo artwork rather than delivery of reusable color specifications.
The client's request for only three logo color versions concerns the independently defined logo-variant Requirement.
The same message separately reports that most PNG logo files do not open properly.
The same message separately discusses inability to open the AI, EPS, and PSD source files.
The same message separately requests identification of the logo lettering and recommendations for complementary fonts.
The request for fonts that complement or match the custom logo lettering also concerns the separate complementary-font recommendation Requirement.
The client explicitly accepts the offer to suggest fonts that complement the logo.
The freelancer commits to compiling and sending complementary font suggestions.
The statement that all logo lettering was custom-made rather than derived from a font supports the separate logo-lettering-basis Requirement.
